Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Bridge team helps businesses build and scale stablecoin-powered financial products and global money movement through a single API. Our virtual accounts let international consumers and businesses access, store, and spend US dollars, while our payouts infrastructure helps platforms disburse funds globally.

We collaborate across product, compliance, legal, and operations as we develop Stripe Crypto’s go-to-market approach and build a durable sales culture. Our team has built financial infrastructure at Coinbase, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, and Airbnb, and we’re focused on making stablecoins a practical foundation for global payments.

What you’ll do

As an Account Executive (New Business), you’ll help grow Bridge by turning qualified demand and outbound prospecting into successful customer relationships. You’ll own the commercial journey from first conversation through launch, translating business and technical needs into practical solutions and working with internal partners to deliver strong outcomes. You’ll also use data and field insights to improve how the team sells and how Stripe Crypto scales.

Responsibilities

  • Close qualified inbound leads and develop outbound opportunities through networking, cold calling, and lead follow-up
  • Lead discovery conversations to understand prospects’ business needs and identify relevant Bridge solutions
  • Manage the full sales cycle, from identifying opportunities through negotiation and close, and partner with customers and internal teams to get them live
  • Build and maintain client relationships that support satisfaction, repeat business, and account growth
  • Meet or exceed monthly, quarterly, and annual sales targets while providing detailed and accurate sales forecasts
  • Collaborate with product, risk, operations, and other internal teams to deliver effective solutions for clients
  • Lead and contribute to team projects that develop and refine the sales process and help shape the Bridge and Stripe sales culture

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 3-8 years of sales experience managing the full sales cycle for new accounts at a high-growth payments, financial technology, crypto, or technology company
  • A track record of exceeding sales quotas, closing net-new and upsell opportunities, and managing complex pricing or commercial negotiations
  • Experience using data to prioritize accounts, build business cases, and track outcomes, including familiarity with customer relationship management tools, Excel, and basic SQL, or demonstrated comfort with comparable data tools and analysis
  • Ability to understand technical product requirements, explain solutions across multiple technology products, and work with product, risk, and operations teams to deliver customer outcomes
  • Strong written and verbal communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to prioritize a high-volume territory and work persistently through ambiguity in a fast-paced environment
  • Enterprise AEs must be in their current role for a minimum of 24 months at the time of application. 
  • Product Sales AE’s must be in their current role for a minimum of 24 months at the time of application.
  • Velocity AEs must be in their current role for a minimum of 18 months at the time of application.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience managing a large book of accounts or a high-velocity sales motion

In-office Expectations

This is an in-office role. Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Opportunity

As OKX continues to expand its products, markets and investment activities, we are looking for a Global Tax Business Partner at Senior Manager level to join our lean, high-impact tax team. The role will partner closely with Product, Finance, Legal, Compliance and Operations teams, to provide commercially practical tax advice, support informed decision-making and ensure that material tax considerations are addressed early and implemented effectively.
 

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Act as the primary tax business partner for the Group’s business globally including its CeFi, Web3, investment arm businesses, building strong relationships with Business, Product, Finance, Legal, Compliance and Operations teams
  • Develop a strong understanding of each business’s products, operating model, fund flows and growth priorities to identify tax considerations early in the decision-making process
  • Partner with the finance BP to determine tax implications of new products, listings, licensing initiatives, new fiat rails and various other initiatives
  • Coordinate the assessment of direct tax, indirect tax, withholding tax, transfer pricing, permanent establishment, nexus and tax-reporting implications, working with Group Tax specialists and external advisers as required. This role owns the business interface: identifying tax issues early, framing commercial options, escalating to the right internal or external SME, and driving approved positions into implementation.
  • Translate complex tax issues into clear commercial implications, practical options and recommendations that enable stakeholders to make informed decisions
  • Work with finance transformation team to establish appropriate tax review gates for material products, transactions and operating-model changes etc and ensure that all material products, listings and market entries receive documented tax sign-off before launch
  • Support the design and implementation of commercially practical and technically supportable entity, contractual, transaction and fund-flow arrangements
  • Work with Finance, Legal, Product, Operations and tax specialists to ensure approved tax positions are implemented consistently in legal agreements, systems, processes, data and accounting treatment
  • Monitor relevant tax legislative, administrative and enforcement developments and proactively assess their impact on the Group’s businesses and planned initiatives
  • Maintain a business tax risk register and documentation of material tax positions, decisions and assumptions, ensuring that identified risks are escalated and remediated on a timely basis
  • Contribute to process improvement initiatives, including enhancement of tax intake processes, documentation standards, knowledge sharing and the use of technology, data analytics or AI in tax workflows
  • Undertake any other tasks and projects assigned.
 

What We Look For In You

  • 10+ years of relevant international tax experience, ideally with a mix of Big 4 or advisoryand in-house roles
  • Broad technical grounding across international tax, permanent establishment and nexus, withholding tax, transfer pricing and indirect tax, with the judgement to identify when specialist advice is required
  • Proven business partnering experience, including advising on new products, transactions, investments, operating-model changes or market-entry initiatives;
  • Strong understanding of commercial and operational considerations, with the ability to translate complex tax issues into practical options and balanced recommendations
  • Experience in digital assets, fintech, financial services, asset management, venture capital or another highly regulated or transaction-driven business is highly preferred
  • Familiarity with crypto is a strong advantage
  • Strong stakeholder-management and communication skills, including the ability to influence senior stakeholders and coordinate cross-functional teams without direct authority
  • Strong analytical and project-management skills, with keen attention to both detail and the bigger picture and the ability to manage multiple priorities across jurisdictions and time zones
  • Self-starter, comfortable operating with ambiguity in a fast-paced, start-up-like environment; resourceful, adaptable and collaborative
  • Demonstrated ability to manage external advisers and drive recommendations through to implementation
  • Familiarity with tax technology, data analytics or AI applications in tax processes is a plus.
 

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • Wellness and meal allowances
  • Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants 
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!

Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose of economic empowerment. The blocks that form our foundational teams — People, Finance, Counsel, Hardware, Information Security, Platform Infrastructure Engineering, and more — provide support and guidance at the corporate level. They work across business groups and around the globe, spanning time zones and disciplines to develop inclusive People policies, forecast finances, give legal counsel, safeguard systems, nurture new initiatives, and more. Every challenge creates possibilities, and we need different perspectives to see them all. Bring yours to Block.

About the Role

As the Director of GTM Strategy & Operations for Third Party Sales & Partner Distribution, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and scaling Square’s third-party and indirect sales ecosystem — spanning independent sales organizations (ISOs), resellers, contractors, distributors, and channel partners across global markets.

You will serve as a strategic and operational business partner to Revenue leadership, working with global and regional leaders to define strategies that expand seller acquisition, improve partner productivity, and accelerate growth through indirect distribution. Your work will ensure these channels have the operating models, insights, and programs needed to deliver consistent, scalable results across diverse markets and partner types.

This role sits within Square’s GTM Strategy & Operations team and partners closely with Sales, Partnerships, Marketing, Finance, Analytics, and operational teams. It is ideal for a strategic operator who blends analytical depth with hands-on execution, thrives in ambiguity, and is excited to build and scale new ways for Square to reach more sellers.

Key Responsibilities

GTM Strategy and Channel Optimization

  • Partner with Revenue leadership to define and execute Square’s global third-party sales and partner distribution strategy, prioritizing the channels, markets, and seller segments with the greatest growth potential.
  • Design partner coverage models, segmentation strategies, and seller engagement frameworks tailored to different partner types and regional needs.
  • Lead annual and quarterly business planning, including growth targets, investment recommendations, capacity planning, and performance expectations.
  • Develop operating models and rules of engagement that support effective collaboration across third-party channels, direct sales, and other partner motions.

Performance and Productivity Acceleration

  • Analyze the partner and seller acquisition funnels to identify performance gaps and improve partner recruitment, activation, ramp time, pipeline generation, and conversion.
  • Develop scalable programs that increase active partner participation, sales productivity, and the volume and quality of sellers acquired through third-party channels.
  • Partner with Finance and Analytics to evaluate channel economics, including acquisition costs, partner incentives, return on investment, and the long-term value of acquired sellers.
  • Establish KPIs, business reviews, and reporting that provide clear visibility into performance across regions and partner types, translating insights into specific actions and accountability.

Cross-Functional GTM Alignment

  • Collaborate with Sales, Partnerships, Marketing, Product, and regional leaders to align third-party distribution strategies with Square’s broader GTM priorities and expansion plans.
  • Partner with Enablement and Marketing to improve partner readiness, lead generation, and adoption of the tools and resources needed to sell Square effectively.
  • Work with Finance, Legal, Compliance, and Operations to develop scalable approaches to partner onboarding, contracting, incentives, and governance.
  • Connect regional teams and global functions to resolve blockers, share best practices, and drive coordinated execution.

AI and Process Innovation

  • Identify opportunities to apply AI and automation to partner prospecting, onboarding, lead qualification, pipeline management, and performance insights.
  • Lead initiatives that simplify partner workflows, strengthen CRM adoption and data quality, and improve visibility into partner-sourced opportunities.
  • Translate business needs into prioritized requirements for systems and tooling partners, supporting implementation and adoption across internal teams and partner channels.
  • Test new processes and tools, measure their impact, and scale approaches that improve productivity and the seller experience.

Strategic Projects and Expansion

  • Lead cross-functional initiatives supporting new markets, new partner models, and growth experiments that expand Square’s distribution and seller reach.
  • Build business cases and financial models to guide investment decisions across emerging and established third-party channels.
  • Develop frameworks for scaling successful programs globally while adapting to local market dynamics, partner capabilities, and channel maturity.
  • Turn ambiguous growth opportunities into clear recommendations, execution plans, and measurable outcomes.

Qualifications

  • 12+ years of experience in Sales Strategy, GTM Strategy & Operations, Business Operations, or Management Consulting, with meaningful experience supporting channel sales, indirect distribution, or partner-led growth.
  • Proven experience designing, optimizing, or scaling third-party sales strategies across multiple markets, regions, or partner models.
  • Strong analytical and financial skills, with experience using data to evaluate growth opportunities, improve sales performance, and guide investment decisions.
  • Understanding of partner economics, incentive structures, sales funnel management, and the drivers of partner activation and productivity.
  • Experience translating strategy into scalable operating models, processes, and programs, including familiarity with CRM systems such as Salesforce and tools that enable automation and performance visibility.
  • Demonstrated ability to partner with senior executives and align cross-functional stakeholders around priorities, decisions, and execution.
  • Ability to balance long-term strategy with hands-on problem-solving, bringing structure to ambiguity and delivering measurable business impact.
  • Experience in payments, FinTech, SaaS, or B2B technology preferred; international experience and familiarity with multiple indirect sales models are highly desirable.

About Bullish

Bullish is an institutionally focused global digital asset platform that provides market infrastructure and information services. These include: Bullish Exchange – a regulated and institutionally focused digital assets spot and derivatives exchange, integrating a high-performance central limit order book matching engine with automated market making to provide deep and predictable liquidity. Bullish Exchange is regulated in Germany, Hong Kong, and Gibraltar. CoinDesk Indices – a collection of tradable proprietary and single-asset benchmarks and indices that track the performance of digital assets for global institutions in the digital assets and traditional finance industries. CoinDesk Data - a broad suite of digital assets market data and analytics, providing real-time insights into prices, trends, and market dynamics. CoinDesk Insights – a digital asset media and events provider and operator of Coindesk.com, a digital media platform that covers news and insights about digital assets, the underlying markets, policy, and blockchain technology.

Reports to:

Vice President, Engineering

Engineering Organization & Culture

At Bullish, we are engineering the institutional standard for the digital asset industry. Our mission is to build a platform centered on security and compliance, requiring a commitment to technical excellence that extends beyond delivering code. As a global organization, we set a high bar for those driven to do their best work alongside experienced, deeply specialized peers. Engineers here treat development as a craft and own the outcome from concept to deployment. Our teams bring structure to ambiguity and shape the frameworks that support a global organization. We refuse to compromise on quality and seek problem solvers who thrive on complex technical challenges with real market consequences.


About the Role & the Team: Trading Product Engineering

The Trading Product Engineering team builds the core distributed systems that drive the global trading experience on Bullish Exchange. We own the end-to-end order lifecycle, orchestrating a hybrid matching engine that combines a Central Limit Order Book with proprietary Automated Market Making, along with the corresponding real-time risk checks and margin requirements. Our systems Our high-throughput APIs enable trading across spot, futures, and options. The work demands absolute correctness in managing complex financial state transitions, translating intricate market structures into scalable solutions.


As a Lead Engineer, Trading Product Engineering, you will drive backend development of the applications, frameworks, and tools at the core of Bullish Exchange. You will design and build high-performance trading and risk components alongside a distributed team based primarily in Hong Kong and Singapore. This is a hands-on technical role with leadership expectations: setting the technical bar, mentoring engineers, and shaping how the team works. Bullish Engineering operates on an AI-first principle, using LLMs throughout the SDLC to speed up development, review, and automation.

What You'll Do:


Engineering & Delivery

  • Design and deliver reusable, reliable, low-latency, low-GC Java code that powers the Exchange, including brokerage, matching, risk and margining components.
  • Apply deep product knowledge across spot and derivatives trading to ensure functional correctness and market fit.
  • Identify bottlenecks and engineer solutions that improve throughput, latency, and reliability.
  • Ensure stability through automated tests at the unit, integration, performance, and stress-testing layers.
  • Own the components the exchange depends on, from design through to production support.

Technical Leadership

  • Set the bar for code quality, automation, and design across the team.
  • Mentor engineers and define what good looks like across the organization.
  • Bring consistent engineering practices across the team's trading systems.


Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate closely with engineers, product, and project management across Hong Kong, Singapore, and other Bullish hubs to decompose complex business requirements into well-tested implementations.


What You'll Bring:

  • 10+ years of Java backend engineering experience, with a focus on front-office execution and trading technologies.
  • Expert-level Java (17+), including the JVM, concurrency primitives, and collections.
  • Experience with low-GC and zero-GC Java programming techniques.
  • Proven track record of architecting and building low-latency trading systems from the ground up.
  • Strong knowledge of event-sourced architecture and messaging technologies such as Aeron, Chronicle Queue, Kafka, RabbitMQ, or Solace.
  • Hands-on experience with Spring or Micronaut, Docker, and Kubernetes.
  • Deep knowledge of testing methodologies, SDLC practices, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Solid understanding of spot, futures, and options markets.
  • Strong mathematical, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Hands-on experience with agentic AI development: LLM integration, prompt engineering, and SDLC automation.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical field.


Nice to Haves:

  • Familiarity with the FIX protocol and related workflows.
  • Experience developing risk systems, such as real-time margin, stress testing, or portfolio exposure, and knowledge of risk methodologies.
  • Experience with backtesting and stress testing.
  • Familiarity with Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
  • Experience in the cryptocurrency or digital asset space.

The Role

We’re looking for an Engagement Marketing Lead to own engagement for Afterpay customers in the US, across the Afterpay app and Afterpay on Cash App, and to extend that work to the commerce and lending products within Cash App, including Cash App Pay and Borrow. More and more customers in the US use both Cash App and Afterpay, and you’ll decide how and when they hear about flexible ways to pay across both products.

The goal is to grow active customers and gross profit by helping people discover, adopt, and keep using flexible ways to pay, through lifecycle programs, cross-sell between Cash App and Afterpay, and the engagement behind new commerce and lending features. You’ll sit on the Engagement Marketing team and act as the senior engagement partner to Afterpay business and product leadership on Afterpay strategy, and to the lending team on overall lending strategy. You’ll also work with Brand and the rest of Growth to drive go-to-market strategy for launches. You’ll trade learnings and best practices with peer teams, including Afterpay International.

Some of this work is well established, with live journeys and a clear measurement history. Some of it has never had a dedicated owner. You’ll decide where to invest, build the opportunity case, and set the roadmap.

What's Unique About This Role

  • The AI frontier. You'll help define how engagement marketing evolves as decisioning and workflow automation take on more of the work, building on automation we already run today.
  • Growth for Afterpay in the US, plus two core verticals. You’ll own the growth strategy for Afterpay in the US and oversee commerce and lending, deciding the right moment to introduce one product versus another to customers who use both Cash App and Afterpay. 
  • Room to define the work. Parts of the commerce and lending experience inside Cash App are open space. You'll size them, prioritize them, and decide what gets built.
  • Economics-led prioritization. We evaluate customer actions by their incremental profit, so the best idea is the one that moves actives and gross profit, not the one that sounds best. You'll make the case for what to invest in and what to leave out.

You Will

  • Partner with Afterpay business and product leadership on Afterpay strategy, and with the lending team on overall lending strategy

  • Push the frontier on AI and automation, helping decide how customer programs evolve as more decisioning is automated
  • Share best practices and learnings with peer engagement teams, including Afterpay International

You Have

  • 8+ years of experience in lifecycle marketing, CRM, growth marketing, growth strategy, business operations, or a consumer-facing analytical role in a B2C tech environment
  • A track record of owning a growth portfolio end-to-end, from opportunity sizing through measurable impact
  • A track record of influencing cross-functional partners without direct authority, including advocating for your recommendation when others see it differently
  • Strong analytical self-sufficiency. You can size an opportunity, build an impact model, and diagnose a program from first principles. Experience with data modeling or opportunity sizing frameworks required; SQL and data visualization experience strongly preferred
  • Experience designing and measuring incentive or offer programs, including incremental impact
  • Hands-on experience with a CRM or marketing automation platform (e.g., Braze, Iterable, Salesforce Marketing Cloud)
  • Strong experimentation experience. You know when to test, when to scale, and when to stop
  • Comfort moving between strategy and hands-on execution
  • Fluency with AI tools as a core part of how you work
  • Clear, takeaway-first communication, including crisp recommendations for senior leadership

Nice to Have

  • Experience in buy now, pay later, lending, payments, or other consumer financial products
  • Experience with commerce, merchant, or partner marketing
  • Experience driving cross-sell between two products or brands
  • Familiarity with regulated or trust-sensitive products (e.g., fintech, financial services, or healthcare)

Technologies We Use and Teach

  • Braze, Iterable, or similar CRM and marketing automation platforms
  • Hightouch or similar audience tools

  • AI tools (Claude Code, Goose, or others) for strategy, execution, and automation

Who we are:

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

Our culture:

  • We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.

  • We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

  • We're a remote-first team spread across time zones, so no office to report to - work from wherever helps you do your best work. Just a couple of things to keep in mind: pay is based on where you're located, and you'll need to keep a home base in the country you're hired in. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible within your country, not borderless.

Location:

  • San Francisco / Hybrid - The role is based in the SF Bay area and we’d require you to be at our Berkeley HQ office at least 2 days per week.

 

About the Role:

Sardine is looking for a Product Lead to lead our efforts around Agentic commerce. Personal Agents have taken the world by storm and this year’s Black Friday and Holiday shopping might be the first one where Agents shop in large numbers.

However, fundamental problems around customer experience, successful conversion, chargeback resolution and fraud prevention still remain. Agents still get blocked by merchants because most Agents behave like Bots. Sardine classifies many AI agents and differentiates them from bots. Sardine’s innovative proposal on Know Your Human allows both agents and merchants to understand the identity of the human behind an agent.

In this role, you will own Sardine’s product on Agentic commerce end-to-end.

This is an ideal role for a prior founder or someone who’s been itching to found something new. We will give you the support and GTM resources to build a new business line from the ground-up.

What you'll be doing

Own the agentic commerce roadmap and build the product that lets merchants welcome trusted AI agents while keeping fraud out:

  • Be directly responsible for the revenue goal for Agentic commerce. We are ambitious and want you and your team to hit $10M ARR in year 1.

  • Own the strategy and roadmap for agentic commerce: identifying AI agents, separating trusted agents from bad bots, and giving merchants clear controls to allow, challenge, or block them.

  • Define success around conversion for legitimate agent traffic, with false positives and fraud loss as the guardrails.

  • Work with data science and engineering on detection signals, models, and the Sardine SDK, and write specs that engineers can build from.

  • Build partnerships across the payments ecosystem, including merchants, PSPs, card networks, and AI agent platforms.

  • Lead go-to-market with the founders and sales: pricing, packaging, design partners, pilots, and launch.

  • Sell and support both enterprises and developers, including developer-first onboarding, documentation, and a self-serve path.

  • Work day to day with the fraud, compliance, and customer teams, and bring customer feedback back into the roadmap.

What you'll need

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with a record of shipping AI products where ML or GenAI capabilities sit inside real user workflows.

  • A strong payments background: card networks, acquiring and issuing, checkout flows, and how fraud and conversion trade off.

  • Fluency with ML concepts such as models, experimentation, metrics, and trade-offs, so you can work closely with data science.

  • Technical depth to design APIs and SDKs and to prototype with AI tools yourself.

  • Experience taking a product to market and selling to both enterprises and developers.

  • Strong analytical skills, and the judgment to balance data with intuition.

  • Clear, direct communication with founders, engineers, and customers.

Bonus

  • Experience in fraud, risk, bot detection, or device intelligence.

  • Founding or early-stage startup experience.

  • Prior work on agentic payments, agent identity, or merchant checkout protocols.

  • Experience running pricing, packaging, and pilot programs for a new product line.

  • SQL or Python skills for your own data analysis.

Interview process

All interviews at Sardine involve a Take Home project. We are sharing what we are looking for in the Take Home.

We want you to code a personal Agent, a wallet or a merchant. We want you to integrate Sardine’s products around fraud prevention. Think of the friction that currently exists in Agentic payments. Then in your project show that friction and also show your proposal on countering that friction. You can view some ideas on how we have vibe coded KYH on the agent side, merchant side or bank side in the demo videos.

If you are interested in applying for this position, please include an idea for what you want to build in your application. After we receive your interest, we will respond back with access to our API docs. Note that our API docs are not public to prevent exposing how we prevent fraud to fraudsters.

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

  • Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

  • Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

Role Roadmap

Accounting Operations will own accounts payable, travel and expense (T&E), and procurement end to end at a high-growth company. Our expenses are large and growing quickly, transaction volume rises every month, and we onboard new vendors at a high and steady clip, so the processes and controls behind spend have to scale with the business. The role is deliberately broad: run these functions day to day, and make them better. This is a hands-on role because we are building the function. You will own the systems, policies, and controls, step into the day-to-day work when it is needed, and improve the process as you go. A core part of the job is developing the AP team: coaching them, raising the bar on quality, and building the procedures and cross-training that let the group run without depending on any one person.

What You’ll Do

Accounts payable

  • Own the full AP cycle: vendor onboarding, invoice coding and approval, payment runs, and vendor inquiries

  • Lead month-end AP close: accruals, reconciliations, and cut-off review

  • Own vendor master data, including bank-detail change controls and 1099 compliance

Travel and expense

  • Own the T&E policy, the expense system, and the corporate card program

  • Oversee expense review and reimbursement; address repeat policy exceptions

Procurement

  • Run the requisition and PO process so spend is approved before it is committed

  • Maintain the approval matrix and partner with budget owners on vendor contracts and renewals

Process improvement and controls

  • Document current processes, find the manual steps and bottlenecks, and fix them

  • Drive automation across AP, T&E, and procurement (invoice capture, workflow routing, ERP integrations)

  • Design and maintain controls over the spend cycle: segregation of duties, approval thresholds, duplicate-payment and vendor-fraud prevention

  • Define and report operating metrics (invoice cycle time, share of spend under PO, exceptions, close timing)

  • Be the point person for auditors on AP, T&E, and procurement

Team development

  • Manage and coach the AP team; set clear goals and give regular feedback

  • Build documented procedures and cross-training so coverage does not depend on one person

  • Act as the escalation point for vendors, employees, and budget owners

What You Bring

  • 5+ years in accounting operations, including time managing AP or a broader procure-to-pay function

  • Have run AP and at least one of T&E or procurement

  • Have improved a process you owned and can point to the results

  • Know the controls that matter in the spend cycle and have put them in place

  • Hands-on with an ERP and an AP automation or expense platform (e.g. NetSuite, Bill.com, Coupa, Ramp, Expensify)

  • Have managed and developed a small team

Preferred qualifications

  • Built a procurement or PO process from end to end

  • Worked at a fast-growing company, building processes designed to scale as volume increased.

NYC Pay Transparency Disclosure

Kalshi has minimal hierarchy and broad variance in experience levels within each title; if your compensation expectations exceed this range, we encourage you to reach out — we’re always happy to discuss.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp's Mid-Market Customer Success Managers on the Lifecycle team don't stop at go-live — they make sure customers keep getting more from Ramp as their business grows. Ramp has grown its product suite significantly over the last several years. As we've matured as an organization, our customer relationships have grown more complex too: customers are buying more of the platform at once, running it across more entities and teams, and relying on it for more of how their finance function operates. Hitting an activation milestone doesn't mean the job's finished. Too often, a feature that could solve a real problem goes unused because no one is there to show how it would work in that customer's business.

That's where you come in. This is a role for people who understand how finance teams actually run, who think in years rather than quarters, and who already use AI the way surgeons use instruments: not occasionally, not as an experiment, but as the default way they work. You'll own the customer experience after implementation for a book of mid-market customers, partnering with Account Management on long-term account strategy. You'll also be one of the first Lifecycle CSMs on a newly formed team, helping define how Ramp earns and keeps the trust of its customers.

What You'll Do

  1. Own the post-implementation experience for a book of mid-market customers, with clear accountability for sustained adoption, customer satisfaction, and renewal readiness

  2. Drive sustained adoption by understanding each customer's goals and guiding them toward the workflows that improve outcomes for their business — including the products and features they've already purchased but haven't fully put to work

  3. Act as each customer's expert in finance workflows: understand how they run their business, advise on decisions as their needs change, and make the value of new Ramp capabilities clear in their context

  4. Build multi-threaded relationships in every account, including finance leadership relationships you own, so the account stays steady through change like a new Controller or CFO

  6. Spot opportunities for growth and bring them to Account Management, who owns renewals and expansion; as customers add products, drive ongoing activation so they reach value quickly

  7. Run your book on data: monitor usage, CP, and risk signals, prioritize where your time goes, and get ahead of challenges and escalations before they reach renewal

  8. Use AI tools daily to prepare for customer calls, build materials, synthesize data, identify account risk, and operate at a pace traditional methods can't match

  9. Bring customer feedback back into Ramp — surfacing patterns, gaps, and opportunities from your accounts to shape how Ramp evolves

  10. Turn what works into repeatable plays, programs, and automations that scale across your book and the team

What You'll Need

  • 5+ years of customer-facing experience in customer success, account management, or consulting, with a proven, consistent track record of retaining customers and exceeding goals

  • Experience owning a book of customers past launch and through renewal, with measurable retention, adoption, or satisfaction results; finance or fintech context is a plus but not required

  • A customer experience mindset — you get ahead of problems before customers raise them and own escalations through resolution

  • AI fluency as a daily habit — you already use AI tools habitually to prep for calls, synthesize information, build customer-facing materials, and automate repetitive tasks; this is how you work, not something you're exploring

  • Ability to communicate Ramp's impact in financial terms — walking a Controller through the value Ramp has delivered and connecting adoption to P&L outcomes

  • A data-driven approach to managing a book — you prioritize based on usage, revenue, and risk signals and can spot an at-risk account well before renewal

  • Technical and systems acumen to understand how Ramp fits into a customer's finance stack, diagnose what's blocking adoption, and bring in the right technical partner

  • A builder mindset — this team is new, and you're energized by shaping the playbooks, programs, and rituals that define how Lifecycle CSMs work while running your own book; you bring structure to ambiguity and iterate quickly

  • Strong collaboration and influencing skills across Sales, Account Management, Product, Operations, and other GTM teams

  2. Exposure to FP&A, accounting software ecosystems (NetSuite, Sage, QuickBooks, Xero), expense management, or CFO-adjacent workflows

TAX OPERATIONS

The Global Tax team’s mission is to support the firm’s compliance with the tax laws and associated reporting obligations of the countries and local jurisdictions in which the firm conducts business. Global Tax analyzes and supports the activities, operations, reporting obligations and transactions of the firm’s business lines so that tax consequences and reputational risks are evaluated appropriately.

###HEADING###OPERATIONS

Operations is a dynamic, multi-faceted function that partners with all areas of the firm to deliver banking, sales and trading, and asset management capabilities to clients around the world. Alongside this service-delivery role, Operations provides essential risk management and control, preserving and enhancing the firm’s assets and reputation. Operations develops the processes and controls and helps specify the systems that deliver accuracy, timeliness and integrity across the business.

###HEADING###YOUR IMPACT

We are seeking an Analyst to join the Tax Operations team to support the firm’s tax reporting obligations, digital transformation, and control governance. In this role, you will develop a deep understanding of core tax systems and processes, applying quantitative rigor and an inquisitive mindset to identify control gaps, remediate processing breaks, and drive sustainable operational improvements. The candidate will be part of the "Change the Bank" initiatives by leveraging BI platforms and AI tools to automate workflows and enhance reporting efficiency. You will collaborate with global teams on critical regulatory tax reform implementations such as FATCA and CRS - while continuously monitoring the regulatory landscape and acting as a regional operational point of contact. Throughout these initiatives, you will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Tax, Legal, Compliance, Controllers, and Business Stakeholders to strengthen the internal control environment, retain critical specialist knowledge, and ensure strict compliance with global tax authorities.

###HEADING###OUR IMPACT

Tax Operations supports the activities, operations, reporting obligations and transactions of the firm’s business lines so that tax consequences and reputational risks are evaluated appropriately. The team manages end-to-end information reporting and withholding governance as well as U.S. and CRS documentation validation, reporting, and Swiss withholding tax reconciliations - while fielding cross-border client tax inquiries. Furthermore, the team evaluates regulatory and business changes to design robust internal controls, partnering closely with Engineering to automate workflows and scale strategic platforms.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • U.S. Information Reporting & QI Compliance: End-to-end reconciliation, withholding tax accounting, and electronic submission of IRS Forms 1042, 1042-S, 1099, and Schedule K-1 packages, ensuring strict Qualified Intermediary (QI) compliance and ledger-to-deposit alignment.
  • Global CRS & U.S. Documentation: Multi-jurisdictional FATCA and CRS reporting programs - overseeing account scoping, XML schema validation, and regulatory filings - while leading annual W-8/W-9/CRS solicitation campaigns to remediate documentation defects, including CRS and U.S. Tax Form validation.

  • Risk Governance & Strategic Transformation: Served as the regional tax operations SME and risk controller, driving control remediation, leading regulatory change initiatives (FATCA/CRS), and optimizing operational tax workflows across global teams.

  • Education & Experience: Bachelor’s degree required, along with 1–3 years of relevant industry experience in financial services, operations, or accounting.
